codes.meaning: The control doesn't register the door as fully latched.
The thermistor (temperature sensor) is reporting something out of range — the specific stage/condition varies by sub-code.
Exhaust airflow is restricted, at increasing severity — almost always a duct or vent blockage.

d80.what_it_means: The dryer has measured restricted exhaust airflow and is telling you the vent is roughly 80% blocked.
d80.why_it_happens: Lint accumulates along the duct run between the dryer and the outside wall. The longer the run and the more bends it has, the faster it builds up.
d80.what_to_try: Clean the lint filter, then disconnect and clear the duct between the dryer and the wall, and check the outside vent flap opens freely. Restricted airflow is the cause in almost every case.
d80.when_to_call: If the whole duct run is clear and the code returns, the sensor or control reading it may be at fault.

d90.what_it_means: The same airflow restriction as d80, but worse -- roughly 90% blocked.
d90.why_it_happens: It is the same lint build-up, caught later. A dryer that reached d80 and was not cleared will usually arrive here.
d90.what_to_try: Treat it as urgent rather than routine: filter, full duct run, and the outside vent. A heavily blocked dryer duct is a fire risk as well as a drying problem.
d90.when_to_call: If clearing the duct does not resolve it, stop using the dryer until it has been checked.

d95.what_it_means: Airflow is restricted to roughly 95%, the most severe level the dryer reports.
d95.why_it_happens: Long-neglected lint build-up, a crushed duct behind the machine, or an outside vent flap that has stopped opening.
d95.what_to_try: Clear the entire duct run rather than just the filter, and confirm the outside vent actually opens when the dryer runs. At this level a partial clean will not clear it.
d95.when_to_call: If the duct is genuinely clear and the code persists, have it looked at before running the dryer again.

codes.meaning: The cycle was interrupted by a power outage.
A gas dryer isn't detecting a gas supply or successful ignition.

cooktop.note: LG treats range/cooktop/oven fault codes as one combined product family documented on a single page.

codes.meaning: Appears on the display when the cooktop surface is still hot (above roughly 150°F), warning not to touch it until it cools.
Flags a problem with the touch-sensitive control pad's sensor circuitry rather than with a heating element itself.
Points to a faulty temperature sensor on the front induction burner.
Signals that the griddle's temperature sensor has failed or is reading incorrectly.
Means the griddle surface isn't reaching or maintaining its set temperature because of a heating malfunction.
Indicates the griddle element is running but failing to properly heat the surface.
Power to the appliance was interrupted, so the clock and any running cycle need resetting.
Not a fault — Sabbath Mode is switched on and is suppressing normal display behaviour.
The front induction burner's temperature sensor is reporting a fault.
The main board and the induction inverter have stopped communicating.
The griddle's temperature sensor circuit is reading as shorted.

oven.note: LG treats range/cooktop/oven fault codes as one combined product family documented on a single page.

codes.meaning: Points to a faulty temperature sensor (thermistor) in the upper oven cavity.
The lower-oven counterpart, flagging a failed thermistor in the bottom cavity on double-oven models.
Means the upper oven's heating circuit isn't functioning correctly.
Shows up when the upper oven is running but not reaching or holding its set temperature.

F9.what_it_means: The upper oven is running but not reaching or holding the temperature it was set to.
F9.why_it_happens: Usually the sensor reporting incorrectly or the heating element not delivering, rather than a setting or a door issue.
F9.what_to_try: Confirm the oven is not in a mode that limits temperature, and that the door is closing fully. Beyond that there is no owner-side check.
F9.when_to_call: If the door seals and the mode is right, the sensor or element needs testing.

codes.meaning: Indicates the self-clean door-lock mechanism on the upper oven has failed to lock or unlock properly.
Appears when the cooling fan stalls or seizes during a self-clean cycle, which can trigger a safety shutdown.
The upper oven's convection fan is not running as the control expects.
The meat-probe circuit is reporting a fault, which can simply mean the probe is not fully seated.
The oven's internal boards have lost communication with one another.

F11.what_it_means: The oven's internal boards have lost communication with one another.
F11.why_it_happens: A wiring or connector fault between boards rather than a cooking fault.
F11.what_to_try: Cut power at the breaker for a minute — that clears a one-off. A code that returns is naming a real fault.
F11.when_to_call: If it comes back after a power cycle, it needs a technician.

codes.meaning: The oven is running but failing to heat the cavity as it should.

F19.what_it_means: The oven is running but failing to bring the cavity up to the temperature it was set to.
F19.why_it_happens: Usually the element not delivering or the sensor misreporting, rather than a setting or a door problem.
F19.what_to_try: Check the door closes fully and the oven is not in a mode that limits temperature. Beyond that there is no owner check.
F19.when_to_call: If the door seals and the mode is right, the element or sensor needs testing.

codes.meaning: The lower oven's door-locking system has failed to lock or release properly.
The supply voltage reaching the range is outside the range it expects.

washer.note: LG publishes separate code lists for front load, top load and pedestal washers. Codes shared across those lists are recorded once here, with a meaning written to hold for all of them.

codes.meaning: The load has settled unevenly in the drum, so the washer cannot reach spin speed safely.

UE.what_it_means: The load has settled unevenly in the drum, so the washer will not take it up to spin speed.
UE.why_it_happens: Normally one heavy item washed alone, or a load that has wrapped into a rope on one side. LG also notes that a load which is too small can trip it, because there is not enough mass to balance.
UE.what_to_try: Redistribute the load by hand. If you are washing a single heavy item, add one or two similar pieces to help it balance, then restart the spin.
UE.when_to_call: If it happens on loads that are clearly well balanced, the suspension or the sensor is worth checking.

codes.meaning: The water cannot drain out, most often because the drain hose is kinked or the pump filter is blocked.

OE.what_it_means: The water cannot drain out of the machine within the time the cycle allows.
OE.why_it_happens: A kinked or clogged drain hose is the cause LG names first. A blocked pump filter does the same thing from inside the machine.
OE.what_to_try: Straighten the drain hose behind the machine and check it is not pushed too far down into the standpipe, then clean the pump filter at the bottom front.
OE.when_to_call: If the hose is clear and the filter is clean, the drain pump needs testing.

codes.meaning: The door is closing but the lock will not engage, which usually points at the latch mechanism rather than the door.

dE2.what_it_means: The door is closing, but the lock will not engage, so the machine will not begin the cycle.
dE2.why_it_happens: Unlike dE1, this usually points at the latch mechanism itself rather than at something caught in the doorway.
dE2.what_to_try: Close the door firmly once more and check nothing is obstructing the latch or the strike. That rules out the simple case.
dE2.when_to_call: If the lock still will not engage with a clear doorway, the latch assembly is the likely fault and needs a technician.

codes.meaning: The door or drawer is not fully closed, so the cycle will not start.

dE1.what_it_means: The door or drawer is not fully closed, so the cycle will not start.
dE1.why_it_happens: Usually laundry caught in the seal, or a door pushed to rather than closed properly.
dE1.what_to_try: Open it fully, clear anything caught around the seal, and close it firmly until it seats.
dE1.when_to_call: If it reads as open with nothing in the way, the door switch is the next thing to check.

codes.meaning: Not enough water is arriving — usually a supply tap that is not fully open, a kinked fill hose, or a blocked inlet screen.

IE.what_it_means: Not enough water is reaching the machine for the cycle it has been asked to run.
IE.why_it_happens: A supply tap that is not fully open, a kinked fill hose, or the inlet screens behind the hoses blocked with scale and grit.
IE.what_to_try: Open both taps fully, straighten the fill hoses, then turn the taps off and check the inlet screens at the machine end for debris.
IE.when_to_call: If supply and screens are both fine, the inlet valve on the machine is the next suspect.

codes.meaning: Not a fault — Child Lock is switched on, so the controls are deliberately ignoring input.

CL.what_it_means: Not a fault. Child Lock is switched on, so the control panel is deliberately ignoring button presses.
CL.why_it_happens: It is normally turned on to stop a running cycle being changed, and then forgotten about.
CL.what_to_try: Hold the Child Lock button — often marked with a padlock, and sometimes a secondary function of another button — for a few seconds to release it.
CL.when_to_call: Only if the lock will not release, which points at the control panel rather than the setting.

codes.meaning: Not a fault — a reminder that the tub clean cycle is due.

tCL.what_it_means: Not a fault. The washer is reminding you that its tub clean cycle is due — a maintenance prompt, not a breakdown.
tCL.why_it_happens: The machine counts wash cycles and raises the reminder after a set number. Front loaders are prone to residue and odour in the door seal and drum if the cycle is never run.
tCL.what_to_try: Run the tub clean cycle with the drum empty, following the detergent guidance in your manual. The reminder clears once the cycle completes.
tCL.when_to_call: No call needed. If the reminder returns immediately after a completed clean cycle, the control is not registering the cycle properly.

codes.meaning: The lid or door is not registering as properly closed, so the washer will not spin.

dE.what_it_means: The washer cannot confirm the lid or door is properly closed, so it will not spin.
dE.why_it_happens: Usually laundry caught in the seal or across the latch, or a door pushed to rather than closed until it seats.
dE.what_to_try: Open fully, clear anything caught around the seal or latch, and close firmly. Check the strike the latch engages for anything bent or obstructing it.
dE.when_to_call: If the doorway is clear and it still reads as open, the door switch or latch assembly needs checking.

codes.meaning: The motor has been overloaded and stalled, typically from too large or too heavy a load.

LE.what_it_means: The motor has been overloaded and stalled, so the washer has stopped rather than keep driving against the load.
LE.why_it_happens: Most often a drum packed too full, or a load that is very heavy when wet — towels, bedding, work clothes.
LE.what_to_try: Take some of the load out, redistribute what is left and restart. Let the machine sit a few minutes first if it has been straining.
LE.when_to_call: If it stalls on normal-sized loads, the motor or its control needs testing.

codes.meaning: Excess suds have been detected, which stops the drum reaching spin speed until they clear.

SUD.what_it_means: Too much foam has built up for the drum to reach spin speed, so the washer pauses to clear it.
SUD.why_it_happens: Usually an overdose of detergent, or a standard detergent in a high-efficiency machine — HE formulas are designed to foam far less.
SUD.what_to_try: Let the suds-clearing routine finish rather than cancelling it. Next load, cut the dose and check the detergent is HE-rated if your machine requires one.
SUD.when_to_call: If it appears with a correct HE dose, something may be holding water in the drum and is worth checking.

codes.meaning: The tub is overfilling, which points at the inlet valve letting water through when it should be closed.

FE.what_it_means: The tub is filling beyond the level it should, so the washer has stopped to avoid overflowing.
FE.why_it_happens: This points at the inlet valve passing water when it has been told to shut, rather than at anything you have done.
FE.what_to_try: Turn the supply taps off at the wall to stop more water arriving. There is no owner-side check that resolves this one.
FE.when_to_call: Straight away. A valve that will not close is a flood risk, not just an error code.

codes.meaning: The cycle was interrupted by a power failure rather than by any fault in the machine.

PF.what_it_means: Not a machine fault. The cycle was interrupted by a power failure and the washer is telling you it stopped partway.
PF.why_it_happens: A cut, a brownout, a tripped breaker, or the plug being pulled mid-cycle.
PF.what_to_try: Restart the cycle. If it recurs without an obvious outage, check the washer is on its own circuit and not sharing with something that draws heavily.
PF.when_to_call: If PF appears repeatedly with no power interruption you can account for, have the supply and the machine's power board looked at.

codes.meaning: The clutch has caught on a foreign object — commonly a coin or clothing fastener that has worked loose.

E6.what_it_means: The clutch has caught on something that should not be in the drum assembly.
E6.why_it_happens: Normally a coin, a button or a clothing fastener that has worked past the drum and lodged where it fouls the mechanism.
E6.what_to_try: Check pockets before washing, and look for anything loose in the drum. If you can see and remove the object, the code may clear.
E6.when_to_call: If nothing is visible, the object has gone somewhere you cannot reach and the machine needs opening.

codes.meaning: The water level sensor is not reporting correctly, so the washer cannot tell how full the tub is.

PE.what_it_means: The water level sensor is not reporting correctly, so the washer cannot tell how full the tub is.
PE.why_it_happens: A sensor or wiring fault, not something caused by the load or the detergent.
PE.what_to_try: A power-cycle at the breaker clears a one-off reading error. There is no other owner-side check here.
PE.when_to_call: If it returns, the pressure sensor needs testing.

codes.meaning: A heating fault, normally traced to the thermistor that reads water temperature.

TE.what_it_means: A heating fault, normally traced to the thermistor that reads water temperature.
TE.why_it_happens: The sensor has drifted or failed, so the control cannot confirm the water reached temperature.
TE.what_to_try: Nothing here is an owner check — the thermistor sits inside the machine.
TE.when_to_call: When you see it. Cold cycles may still run, but the machine is not doing what the programme selected.

codes.meaning: The door latch itself is malfunctioning rather than simply being obstructed.

dL.what_it_means: The door latch itself is malfunctioning rather than simply being obstructed.
dL.why_it_happens: Unlike dE1, this points at the mechanism rather than at laundry caught in the doorway.
dL.what_to_try: Close the door firmly once with nothing in the way, to rule out the simple case.
dL.when_to_call: If it still will not lock with a clear doorway, the latch assembly needs replacing.

codes.meaning: An over-current condition in the electrical circuit has shut the cycle down.
